lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Q3 US same-store sales are more likely to print below the 1.1% published consensus, central estimate about +0.6%. Wells Fargo's 2026-10-06 note says Q3 card spending slowed 120bp quarter on quarter. BofA card data showed pizza sales declining over May-July 2026, with lower-income pizza spending down most. Kalshi, the only market quoting the line, repriced 'above 0.5%' from 0.83-0.99 in late September to 0.40, and 'above 1.5%' from 0.66 in August to about 0.15.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: US SSS +0.1% against about 0.6% expected, guide held, stock +2.1% (premarket +6.5-8%, https://www.rttnews.com/3668360/domino-s-pizza-shares-climb-on-higher-q2-profit-orders-u-s-comps-edge-up.aspx). Q1 2026: +0.9% against about 2.7% with a guide cut, -8.8%. Q3 2025: +5.2% beat, +3.9%. Q4 2025: +3.7%, +4.1%. This name has bought a comp miss when orders grew and the guide held.

findings.finding: H1 US comps were +0.5%. If Q3 prints about 0.6%, keeping the FY26 'low single digits' guide needs Q4 (16 weeks, lapping +3.7%) at about 2% to reach a 1% year, so an explicit trim on new CEO Joe Jordan's first call is close to a coin flip. Three things offset it: Wells' card data says Q4-to-date is stronger (the Domino launched Aug 31, a Labor Day shift, a 50%-off week Oct 5-11), BofA shows September consumer spending +6.2% y/y with lower-income households at +5.5%, and Jordan is an insider with no reset signalled.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: US comp guide cut from about 3% to 'low single digits', -8.8%. Q2 2026: guide held after a comp miss, +2.1%. The guide line has decided the sign on both 2026 prints.

findings.finding: International ex-FX comps should land at +0.5% to +1.5% against the +1.0-1.2% modelled, with a slight upside lean. Jubilant's Domino's India like-for-like was +4.1% for Jul-Sep 2026, up from +2.5% (2026-10-07). DPG UK posted H1 +4.9% with July positive on the World Cup, against an easy +1.0% Q3-2025 lap. Domino's Pizza Enterprises' run-rate is unchanged: FY26 was -4.1%, and the first 8 weeks of FY27 were -5.8% per a secondary source. DPC Dash's Q3 comps are still negative, but its ticket is stabilising.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: international -0.1% against about +0.5% expected, stock still +2.1%. The international line has not led the reaction.

findings.finding: Reported EPS carries a DPC Dash mark-to-market loss that consensus does not model. The 10-Q shows ~3.9m shares at HK$35.58 ($17.7m) on 2026-06-14, and 1405.HK closed at HK$30.50 on 2026-09-04. That is about -$2.5m pre-tax, or about -$0.06 a share after tax. It is partly offset by an international royalty consensus (Zacks $78.5m, -0.1% y/y) that looks low next to Q2's +6.0% y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a $12.4m DPC Dash loss (~$0.29) turned an EPS beat into a $4.07 vs $4.17 headline miss, and the stock still rose 2.1% (https://streetsignal.substack.com/p/dpz-earnings-bridge-f3q26). Headline EPS has not driven this name's reaction.

lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): DPZ bought a 0.5pt comp miss in Q2 2026 (+2.1%) when orders grew and the guide held, so the reaction function shrinks the Q1 finding: -0.8 to about -0.55.

Lesson 5 (narrow proxy against a broad series; documents beat inference): re-read the Wells sentence. Its card-data figure is not stated as DPZ-specific, and Wells reconciles it to +90bp of acceleration. Kept the more direct series (DPZ and pizza card data) above the broad Census and BofA restaurant acceleration, but the weaker proxy plus the netted counter-evidence takes Q1 to -0.4 and moves the central comp from +0.4% to +0.6% (print_vs_bar -0.7 to -0.5).
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the comp bar is disputed (Zacks 1.1%, other models 0.72-1.0%, Kalshi ~0.3%), so every finding stays capped small and p_up moves toward 50.

Lesson 7 (positioning): the negative sign runs against a call-bid skew (-10.5) I cannot argue is wrong, so Q1 goes -0.4 to -0.3 and Q2 -0.2 to -0.1. Short interest is 7.8% with 3.1 days to cover and falling, not crowded, so no further squeeze cut.
Lesson 2 (name the line; one-offs at a fraction): Q4's DPC Dash mark is filed as a one_off at a fraction (-0.1), unchanged.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number) and reading the set: Q1 and Q2 carry their counter-evidence net in the size. No two findings contradict each other, and none shares a fact.

Pessimism artefact: three of four findings lean negative, so I re-checked the positive evidence (Census, BofA September, Google Q3, Jubilant, DPG, share donors). It is sized in, and the net sum of -0.30 is near zero.

Scaled measurement: p_up 46 to 48 (lessons 1, 6 and 7 each toward 50, applied once). abs_move 6.0 to 6.5, because a guidance change on a new CEO's first call is likely and the hunters' sizes have run small (core table). expected_move goes from -0.48 to -0.26.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sales beats have not been paid. Q2-26 beat ~1.2% with a raise: -2.69% (MedTech/HCA day). Q1-26 beat: +0.90%. Q4-25 in line: -0.09%. Q3-25 beat ~1%: -0.03% (baseline history; The Star 2026-07-17).

findings.finding: The July guide assumed EUR 1.15; the euro is at 1.116 (2026-10-12). That is ~-$0.17bn on Q4 European sales and ~-$0.02-0.03 of EPS. FY consensus already sits at $101.38bn revenue (top of the $100.8-101.4bn range) and $11.085 EPS (above the $11.035 midpoint). So even with an operational raise, the reported FY26 midpoint likely lands ~$101.1-101.3bn and ~$11.04-11.08: in line to slightly below the street, a flow-through raise rather than one beyond it.

findings.finding: Q3 adjusted EPS carries Firefly's ~$1bn IPR&D (~$0.41-0.46/share, 'in 3Q26'). J&J's 2026-09-16 phasing note says the FY26 deal impacts 'primarily relate to transactions completed and/or entered into during Q3 2026'. If Sail's ~$0.13-0.18 also lands in Q3, the print is ~$2.40-2.48 against a $2.53 mean that spans $2.31-2.81, a mechanical headline miss on a charge already in the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS surprises have barely moved JNJ: +1.5% beat -0.03%, -0.1% in line -0.09%, +0.85% beat +0.90%, +1.58% beat -2.69% (Yahoo earningsHistory vs baseline moves).

findings.finding: On 2026-09-09 the MedTech chief was asked to confirm H2 growth above H1 excluding the extra week. He did not. He cited tougher Q3/Q4 comps, 'lingering challenges around competitive intensity' in EP (outside the US), Middle East disruption and China EP VBP 'later this year', then pivoted to the enterprise guide. With Q2 EP at +3.1% against a +9.7% Q3-25 comp and Abiomed at -2% against +15.6% (Class I Impella recall, FDA 2026-07-02), MedTech operational growth is more likely ~3-4% than an acceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2-26 MedTech/Impella miss 'overshadowed' an IM-led beat and raise: -2.69% on 2026-07-15, the same day HCA warned on surgical volumes (The Star, 2026-07-17).

outside_window.finding: 2027 colour at the 2026-12-08 Enterprise Business Review: ICOTYDE peak, oncology '$50bn should be the floor', 2027 'stronger than 2026'. Also whether Sail's option is exercised, which carries a $1.28 2027 EPS charge; the FY27 EPS mean of $12.375 spans $11.05-13.47 on it.

The $5.5bn ovarian talc settlement needs 95% participation of ~76,000 claims, with no deadline stated; the MDL show-cause order on specific causation (2026-07-22) is pending. Finalisation would remove the overhang; any reserve change is GAAP-only.
Orthopaedics (DePuy Synthes) separation is targeted for mid-2027, with the ~$20bn Apollo talks reported 2026-09-11. If no agreement comes on 10/13, the resolution is later.

findings.finding: Fuel costs rose well above the levels at which the 23 Jul FY26 guide was set: US diesel went from $5.13-5.31 to a $6.53 peak on 21 Sep and $6.20 on 5 Oct (+66% y/y), Brent from ~$83-96 to $124 (18 Sep) and $120 (2 Oct), and California regular from ~$5.35-5.49 to $6.23. ACI's own Q1 10-Q names higher fuel costs as a gross-margin drag at +47% y/y diesel, and the guide already needs adj EBITDA to improve from ~-9% y/y (Q1, guided Q2) to ~-4% in H2 at the midpoint (52-week basis). That lifts the chance of a trim or a 'low end' steer above what a FY consensus flat at $1.79 for 60 days holds. Net of Kroger holding its profit guide on 11 Sep with diesel included, management's late-July share buying and RBC's call for a hold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide cut 2026-07-23 (EPS $2.22-2.32 to $1.75-1.85, IDs to -1.5/-0.5): stock -21.6%. Guide raised 2025-10-14 (IDs 2.2-2.75%, EPS $2.06-2.19): stock +13.6% (baseline history; Q2 FY25 release).

findings.finding: Census advance data show grocery-store sales (seasonally adjusted) slowing to +0.6% y/y in July and +0.5% in August, from +2.4% in May and about +1.0% for January-June, with CPI food-at-home at +2.2%. Add the IRA step-up embedded in ACI's own guide (~100bp in Q1, ~150bp for the year, so ~170bp for Q2-Q4) and the tougher pharmacy compares management flagged from Q2. Q2 identical sales are then more likely -1.3% to -1.8% than RBC's -1%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 IDs -0.8% came with the guide cut (-21.6%); Q2 FY25 IDs +2.2% came with a raised ID guide (+13.6%). The ID line has moved this stock only together with the guide. The closest template, Kroger on 11 Sep (ID miss, ID guide cut, profit guide held), was bought: KR +2.7% and +4.1% over two sessions.

findings.finding: Retail fuel margins were strong through most of ACI's Q2 window. Kroger's fuel profit per gallon rose slightly in its quarter to 15 Aug, Casey's earned 47.8c/gal in May-July against 41.0c a year earlier, and Q2 diesel was +39% y/y against +47% in Q1. The CFO's 'Q2 adj EBITDA very similar to Q1 y/y' (~$770M consensus, ~$0.33 EPS on my bridge) therefore looks reachable, rather than RBC's $761M (~$0.315).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 FY26 EPS miss ($0.42 vs $0.54) compounded the guide cut (-21.6%). A quarter that lands on what management guided has not moved this name by itself.

outside_window.finding: The Delaware Chancery trial of Albertsons' suit against Kroger (the $600M termination fee plus damages, including the lost shareholder premium; Bloomberg on 12 Oct reports ACI seeks more than $9B against a ~$6.0B market cap) begins 2026-10-19, after the exit window. A ruling comes later. A settlement announced before the trial is a low-probability, large positive tail that nothing found suggests is imminent.

Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name trades the ID line only through the guide, and Kroger's ID miss with profit held was bought): F2 cut from -0.5 to -0.4
